paragraphs.text: Thin-client Android reader for Calibre + FanFicFare + Kokoro TTS (Tauri v2 + Svelte 5)
# Calaloud

A **thin client** Android (Tauri v2) reader for fanfic and ebooks. It does **not**
bundle or host an

y service — it only *connects* to three separately-run services the
user already has, each with its
own codebase/docker image:
| Service | Role |

| **Calibre content server** | Book library (per-user libraries), EPUB download, progress column |
|

**Kokoro TTS** (OpenAI-compatible) | Default narration voice |
| **FanFicFare-as-a-service** | Turn
s a story URL into an EPUB |

The client is a **Svelte 5 UI wrapped in Tauri v2** producing an **Android APK** (a
desktop build is

optional, same UI). It keeps the reader, library shelf, narration
playback, and an offline cache. A

ll service-side logic (`calibredb`, FanFicFare worker,
TTS model) stays out of the binary.

User experience is modeled on the **Webnovel app** (library/shelf UX) and **Librera
Reader** (reader
ergonomics), with **Kokoro TTS** as the default voice.

ding the Android APK.

ng the Android APK.
- `docs/docker-compose.services.yml` — reference Compose for the three services.

## Status
Working Android client (Tauri v2). Builds and installs as an APK; see
`docs/build.md` and
`docs/TODO.md` for what's done and what's next.

## Quick facts
- **Thin client:** the app only points at user-configured service endpoints in Settin

gs
(Calibre, Kokoro, FanFicFare) — nothing service-side is bundled.
- **Stack:** Svelte 5 + Vite + T

ypeScript frontend; Tauri v2 native shell; IndexedDB
offline cache; FanFicFare / Calibre / Kokoro HT

TP clients.
- **Dev environment:** Nix dev-shell (`nix develop`) provides Rust with Android
targets,
Android SDK + NDK + JDK 17, and `cargo-tauri`.
